messages:
sarah (support): FYI customer reported repeated 504s and p95 skyrocketing on hosted inference. They say calls time out at ~30s and some return 502/504. attaching snippet from their side: 

casey (product): link to trace they sent: https://acme.example/traces/8f3e

sarah (support): @mike (eng-runtime) can you triage? customer says issue started after a traffic burst ~09:12 UTC, continuous batching backlog suspected.

mike (eng-runtime): looking. I can see gateway 5xx spikes in our telemetry around 09:12. p50 fine, p95/p99 huge. opening tail traces now.

jess (eng-sre): I see queue-depth metric jump on hostpool-3 and queue-dequeue latency increase. Possibly continuous-batcher backlog + tenant kv cache spin-up.

anil (oncall): any quick mitigations? customer is high-tier.

mike (eng-runtime): can we temporarily reduce max_batch_size for hosted-tier to force smaller batches? Also consider lowering batching window.

casey (product): customer is on Redwood Hosted, model redwood-13b-8q. They hit a burst of 250 rps sustained for ~2m. Their requests are longseq (tokens ~1200).

sarah (support): repro steps from customer: 
1) concurrent 400 requests over 90s 
2) seq len ~1200 
3) status: many 504s after 25-35s

mike (eng-runtime): got a repro in staging with a synthetic client. Observed continuous-batcher queue depth climb to 4800 requests, dequeue rate couldn't catch up because each batch execution took ~2.8s for these seq lengths. KV cache warmup added CPU pressure.

jess (eng-sre): stack traces show dequeue worker saturation and some workers hitting backoff due to GC. Also our ingress limiter began early rejecting tenant at ~09:14 which caused retry spirals.

anil (oncall): rolling a quick hotfix: lower continuous-batching.window_ms from 40 to 15 for hosted pool and set max_batch_size to 64. @deploy-bot kick? :pray:

deploy-bot: deploy started by anil (oncall) — rolling config change to hosted-batcher pool in us-west-2.

mike (eng-runtime): applying a per-tenant queue depth cap patch (soft-limit) to avoid one tenant monopolizing the batcher. This will drop excess requests early with clear 429 so client can retry with backoff.

sarah (support): applied customer-facing mitigation: asked them to reduce concurrency and enable exponential backoff. also opened a billing note to avoid overcharges during retries.

mike (eng-runtime): after changes p95/tail dropped from 7.4s -> 1.1s in 2m window. 5xxs trended down to baseline. We still see some KV cache spinups causing spikes — scheduling follow-up.

jess (eng-sre): creating follow-up incident runbook items: 
- add tenant-aware queue-depth metrics to dashboards
- auto-throttle when dequeue lag > 2x normal
- avoid silent early-late 5xx by returning 429 when queue soft-limit hit
- improve KV-cache parallelism during warmup

casey (product): also flagging for product: consider adding client-side recommended headers for expected seq-len and preferred latency class so our router can pick cheaper, smaller-batch paths.

anil (oncall): postmortem notes: root cause = request queue saturation from longseq traffic spike + continuous-batcher window tuned for throughput not extreme tails; exacerbated by KV-cache warmups and ingress retry amplification. Mitigations implemented: batcher window reduction, max_batch_size cap, per-tenant queue soft-limits, customer communication.

sarah (support): customer acknowledged and will test with lower concurrency. they asked for a follow-up with timeline to prevent recurrence.

mike (eng-runtime): we'll schedule a small rollout: new batching defaults in hosted for longseq detection and per-model batching profiles. I'll add a canary to 10% of hosts tomorrow.

jess (eng-sre): tagging runbook: add alert when queue-depth > 3000 for >30s, and create a runbook step to trigger immediate narrow-batch fallback.

anil (oncall): closing incident channel after we confirm 24h stability. assigning owners: mike -> runtime fixes, jess -> alerts/runbook, casey -> product follow-up, sarah -> customer comms.

sarah (support): thanks team :thumbsup:
